title: Human impersonator - port-out attempt on Marcus Webb
summary: A fraudster with stolen account details calls in their own voice to move the number to another carrier. The anti-spoofing model rightly hears a real human, but the voiceprint says it is not the account holder. Shield switches to a question from the account history, the caller cannot answer, and the real customer taps 'Not me' on the phone on file.

voices.caller: Real human voice, not the account holder: LibriSpeech dev-clean speaker 3752 (CC BY 4.0)

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you for calling, this is Oliver. Am I speaking with the account holder, Marcus Webb?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thanks. I see you'd like a PIN to move your number to another carrier. May I ask why you're leaving us?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Understood. Moving a number is a high risk change, so first, one quick question from your account history. Which phone did you get from us in August?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Then don't you interfere with me, sir.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I'm sorry, I can't issue a port-out PIN without verification. I've sent a confirmation request to the phone on the account. Please approve it there.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: I'll show you who's master here, my good sir.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: The account holder has just tapped Not me on that phone. I can't make any changes on this call, and this request is now closed.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: I'll report this to the government.
